body.title: Your people await you
paragraphs: Time. A game day passes every 30 minutes. Game days begin after 1 Wanaxes join.

Foot soldiers cross a plains hex in 1 game day, olive woodland in 1.5, hills or cedar forest in 2, desert in 3. War chariots cross plains in 0.67 game day but need 2 in olive woodland and 3 in hills, cedar forest or desert. A full-crewed galley crosses 3 coastal or 5 open-sea hexes a game day.
Your Host carries 1200 grain and 120 silver. It lives on subsistence until founding; these reserves do not drain. Find your place — founding is final.
Food first. A city must feed itself. Starvation makes it shrink; below 50 people it falls.

The gods. A new Wanax starts at 40 Kharis. It fades slowly from the start; each additional city increases the daily cost, even with a temple. A temple takes 16 game days to build: staff and feed it to earn favour. Low standing risks punishment.
Place citizens on olive woodland or cedar forest for timber, and on stone-bearing ground for stone; idle citizens produce nothing.
Orders travel. A Runner must reach a unit in the field before it follows your new order.
Bronze needs others. Copper and tin lie on separate landmasses; trade, colonies or seizures can bring them together.
